"""
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  THE ONE DAG — your ONLY reference for live coding                         ║
║                                                                            ║
║  Stop looking at other files. This is the one you memorize.                ║
║  Insurance claims domain (matches Capgemini's US insurer client).          ║
║  Uses ONLY TaskFlow API (@dag + @task decorators).                         ║
║  Production-ready: sensors, validation, processing, QC, notifications.    ║
║                                                                            ║
║  PRACTICE PLAN:                                                            ║
║  1. Read this ONCE top to bottom                                           ║
║  2. Close file → open blank file → write from memory                       ║
║  3. Compare, fix mistakes, repeat                                          ║
║  4. Goal: write it in 10 minutes while explaining every line               ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

THE STRUCTURE IS ALWAYS THE SAME — memorize this shape:

    IMPORTS → DEFAULT_ARGS → @dag → SENSOR → @tasks → NOTIFICATIONS → WIRING

That's it. Every production DAG follows this skeleton.
"""

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 1: IMPORTS  (say: "I'll start with the imports I need")
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TIP: In the interview, write imports as you need them.
# Don't try to memorize all — add each when you use the class.

from datetime import datetime, timedelta                          # scheduling
from airflow.decorators import dag, task                          # TaskFlow API
from airflow.providers.amazon.aws.sensors.s3 import S3KeySensor   # wait for file
from airflow.providers.amazon.aws.hooks.s3 import S3Hook           # interact with S3
from airflow.providers.snowflake.hooks.snowflake import SnowflakeHook  # query Snowflake
from airflow.operators.email import EmailOperator                  # send alerts
from airflow.utils.trigger_rule import TriggerRule                 # conditional execution
import subprocess
import json
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# using EmrAddStepsOperator instead of spark-submit for better integration with EMR cluster (monitoring, retries, logging)
"""
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from airflow.decorators import dag, task
from airflow.providers.amazon.aws.operators.emr import EmrAddStepsOperator
from airflow.providers.amazon.aws.sensors.emr import EmrStepSensor

# Constantes de Produção (Geralmente externalizadas em variáveis de ambiente ou Airflow Variables)
CLUSTER_ID = "j-2AL3XXXXXX89"  # ID do seu cluster EMR persistente ou dinâmico
AWS_CONN_ID = "aws_capgemini_production"
S3_ARTIFACTS_BUCKET = "s3://capgemini-data-artifacts-prod/spark-scripts"

# Definição dos Steps do Spark (o "esqueleto" do comando)
def get_spark_steps(execution_date):
    return [
        {
            "Name": f"Processamento_Claims_{execution_date}",
            "ActionOnFailure": "CONTINUE",  # CONTINUE ou CANCEL_AND_WAIT
            "HadoopJarStep": {
                "Jar": "command-runner.jar",
                "Args": [
                    "spark-submit",
                    "--deploy-mode", "cluster",  # Em prod, DRIVER roda no cluster, não no client!
                    "--master", "yarn",
                    "--conf", "spark.executor.memory=8g",
                    "--conf", "spark.driver.memory=4g",
                    "--conf", "spark.executor.cores=4",
                    "--conf", "spark.sql.shuffle.partitions=400",
                    # Caminho do script centralizado no S3
                    f"{S3_ARTIFACTS_BUCKET}/process_claims.py",
                    # Argumentos dinâmicos enviados para o sys.argv do script
                    "--source", f"s3://capgemini-raw-prod/claims/{execution_date}/",
                    "--target", f"s3://capgemini-trusted-prod/claims/",
                    "--date", execution_date
                ],
            },
        }
    ]

default_args = {
    "owner": "data-engineering-team",
    "depends_on_past": False,
    "retries": 2,
    "retry_delay": timedelta(minutes=5),
}

@dag(
    dag_id="prod_emr_spark_process_claims",
    default_args=default_args,
    start_date=datetime(2026, 1, 1),
    schedule="@daily",
    catchup=False,
    tags=["production", "emr", "spark", "claims"],
)
def emr_pipeline():

    @task
    def get_execution_date(**kwargs):
        # Captura a data lógica de execução da DAG em formato string (Ex: 2026-06-10)
        return kwargs['ds']

    # 1. Task que adiciona o Step ao EMR
    # Note o uso de Jinja Template para injetar os steps gerados dinamicamente
    add_spark_step = EmrAddStepsOperator(
        task_id="add_spark_step_to_emr",
        job_flow_id=CLUSTER_ID,
        aws_conn_id=AWS_CONN_ID,
        steps=get_spark_steps("{{ ds }}"), # Jinja avalia a data de execução automaticamente
    )

    # 2. O Sensor que monitora se o step terminou com sucesso
    # Em produção, DEFERRABLE=TRUE é obrigatório para não travar workers do Airflow por horas
    monitor_spark_step = EmrStepSensor(
        task_id="monitor_spark_step",
        job_flow_id=CLUSTER_ID,
        step_id="{{ task_instance.xcom_pull(task_ids='add_spark_step_to_emr')[0] }}",
        aws_conn_id=AWS_CONN_ID,
        deferrable=True, # Modo assíncrono inteligente
        poke_interval=30
    )

    # Fluxo de execução
    execution_date = get_execution_date()
    execution_date >> add_spark_step >> monitor_spark_step

emr_pipeline()
"""
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 2: DEFAULT_ARGS  (say: "These apply to every task in the DAG")
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

DEFAULT_ARGS = {
    "owner": "data-engineering",
    "depends_on_past": False,          # each run independent
    "retries": 2,                      # retry twice on failure
    "retry_delay": timedelta(minutes=5),
    "retry_exponential_backoff": True,  # 5min → ~10min → capped
    "max_retry_delay": timedelta(minutes=30),
    "email_on_failure": True,
    "email_on_retry": False,            # avoid alert fatigue
    "email": ["data-team@company.com"],
}


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 3: @dag DECORATOR  (say: "Now I define the DAG itself")
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

@dag(
    dag_id="claims_daily_pipeline",
    default_args=DEFAULT_ARGS,
    description="Daily insurance claims: S3 → validate → process → Snowflake → QC",
    schedule="0 6 * * *",              # daily at 6 AM UTC
    start_date=datetime(2026, 1, 1),   # ← datetime, NOT timedelta
    catchup=False,                     # don't backfill past runs on deploy
    max_active_runs=1,                 # prevent overlapping runs
    tags=["claims", "daily", "production"],
)
def claims_daily_pipeline():
    """
    Insurance claims pipeline — daily ingestion from S3 landing zone
    through validation, processing, and quality checks into Snowflake.
    """

    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # STEP 4: SENSOR  (say: "First, I wait for the source file in S3")
    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # "Sensors are the gatekeepers — nothing downstream runs until
    #  the file lands. I use reschedule mode so the worker slot is
    #  freed between checks instead of blocking for hours."

    wait_claims_file = S3KeySensor(
        task_id="wait_claims_file",
        bucket_name="insurance-landing",
        bucket_key="claims/{{ ds }}/claims.json",  # {{ ds }} = execution date
        aws_conn_id="aws_default",
        poke_interval=300,     # check every 5 min
        timeout=14400,         # fail after 4 hours
        deferrable=True,       # release worker slot between checks
        #mode="reschedule",     # free worker between checks - how we are using deferrable=True its retundand
    )

    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # STEP 5: VALIDATE SOURCE  (say: "Before expensive processing,
    #   I validate the file — fail fast, save money")
    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

    @task()
    def validate_source(ds: str = None) -> dict:
        """
        Check source file exists and has valid size.
        head_object = metadata only, no download.
        """
        hook = S3Hook(aws_conn_id="aws_default")
        key = f"claims/{ds}/claims.json"

        # head_object returns metadata without downloading the file
        metadata = hook.head_object(key=key, bucket_name="insurance-landing")
        size_mb = metadata["ContentLength"] / (1024 * 1024)

        if size_mb < 0.001:
            raise ValueError(f"File too small: {size_mb:.4f} MB — likely empty")
        if size_mb > 5000:
            raise ValueError(f"File too large: {size_mb:.1f} MB — investigate")

        logger.info("Source validated: %s (%.2f MB)", key, size_mb)

        # Return metadata dict → automatically pushed to XCom
        # Downstream tasks receive this as a function argument
        return {
            "source_path": f"s3://insurance-landing/{key}",
            "size_mb": round(size_mb, 2),
            "date": ds,
        }

    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # STEP 6: PROCESS  (say: "Main transformation — in production
    #   this calls spark-submit; the DAG is the orchestrator, not the
    #   processing engine")
    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

    @task()
    def process_claims(source_info: dict) -> dict:
        """
        Process claims data. DAG = orchestrator (lightweight).
        Heavy logic lives in external Spark script.
        XCom carries paths and counts, NEVER raw data.
        """
        cmd = [
            "spark-submit",
            "--master", "yarn",
            "--deploy-mode", "cluster", # in prod the driver should run on the cluster, not the Airflow worker
            "--conf", "spark.executor.memory=4g",
            "--conf", "spark.sql.shuffle.partitions=200",
            "/opt/airflow/scripts/process_claims.py",
            "--source", source_info["source_path"],
            "--date", source_info["date"],
        ]

        logger.info("Submitting Spark job: %s", " ".join(cmd))
        proc = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=7200)

        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Spark failed (exit {proc.returncode}): {proc.stderr[-2000:]}")

        # Convention: Spark script prints JSON summary on last stdout line
        for line in reversed(proc.stdout.strip().split("\n")):
            try:
                return json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue

        return {"status": "success", "records": 0, "date": source_info["date"]}

    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # STEP 7: LOAD TO SNOWFLAKE  (say: "After processing, I load
    #   the results into Snowflake using the SnowflakeHook")
    #
    # There are 3 ways to load data into Snowflake from Airflow.
    # I'm using Level 1 (Hook) here because I need Python logic around
    # the SQL. Below I show Level 2 and Level 3 as commented alternatives.
    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # LEVEL 1: SnowflakeHook inside @task (WHAT WE USE HERE)
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # When: need Python logic around the SQL (dynamic queries, check
    #       results, branch, build query from XCom data)
    # Hook = low-level connector. YOU write the SQL + control flow.

    @task()
    def load_to_snowflake(process_info: dict) -> dict:
        """
        Load processed data into Snowflake.
        MERGE = idempotent: safe to retry without duplicating data.
        Hook manages credentials via Airflow connection — never hardcoded.
        """
        hook = SnowflakeHook(snowflake_conn_id="snowflake_default")

        # MERGE (upsert) = idempotent: same result if run once or ten times
        hook.run(f"""
            MERGE INTO claims_warehouse.claims_daily AS target
            USING claims_staging.claims_raw AS source
            ON target.claim_id = source.claim_id
               AND target.claim_date = '{process_info["date"]}'
            WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET
                status = source.status,
                amount = source.amount,
                updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
            WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (
                claim_id, claim_date, status, amount, created_at
            ) VALUES (
                source.claim_id, source.claim_date, source.source_status,
                source.amount, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
            )
        """)

        # Verify row count after load
        result = hook.get_first(f"""
            SELECT COUNT(*) FROM claims_warehouse.claims_daily
            WHERE claim_date = '{process_info["date"]}'
        """)
        row_count = result[0] if result else 0

        logger.info("Loaded %d rows for date %s", row_count, process_info["date"])
        return {
            "status": "loaded",
            "row_count": row_count,
            "date": process_info["date"],
        }

    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # LEVEL 2: SnowflakeOperator (ALTERNATIVE — commented)
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # When: SQL is static or uses only Jinja templates. No Python logic
    #       needed. Cleaner when SQL lives in a separate .sql file.
    #
    # The SQL file lives in a separate folder, NOT inside the DAG:
    #
    #   project/
    #   ├── dags/
    #   │   └── claims_daily_pipeline.py     ← this DAG file
    #   └── include/
    #       └── sql/
    #           └── merge_claims.sql         ← SQL file here
    #
    # On Astronomer, "include/" is the standard folder for SQL, configs,
    # scripts. It gets deployed alongside dags/ automatically.
    #
    # from airflow.providers.snowflake.operators.snowflake import SnowflakeOperator
    #
    # # Option A: SQL inline (short queries)
    # merge_claims = SnowflakeOperator(
    #     task_id="merge_claims",
    #     snowflake_conn_id="snowflake_default",
    #     sql="""
    #         MERGE INTO claims_warehouse.claims_daily AS target
    #         USING claims_staging.claims_raw AS source
    #         ON target.claim_id = source.claim_id
    #            AND target.claim_date = '{{ ds }}'
    #         WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET
    #             status = source.status,
    #             amount = source.amount,
    #             updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
    #         WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (
    #             claim_id, claim_date, status, amount, created_at
    #         ) VALUES (
    #             source.claim_id, source.claim_date, source.status,
    #             source.amount, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
    #         )
    #     """,
    # )
    #
    # # Option B: SQL from file (cleaner for complex queries)
    # # Airflow resolves the path relative to the DAG file or dags/ folder.
    # # {{ ds }} inside the .sql file is rendered by Jinja at runtime.
    # merge_claims = SnowflakeOperator(
    #     task_id="merge_claims",
    #     snowflake_conn_id="snowflake_default",
    #     sql="include/sql/merge_claims.sql",   # ← path to .sql file
    # )
    #
    # # The .sql file (include/sql/merge_claims.sql) would contain:
    # # MERGE INTO claims_warehouse.claims_daily AS target
    # # USING claims_staging.claims_raw AS source
    # # ON target.claim_id = source.claim_id
    # #    AND target.claim_date = '{{ ds }}'
    # # WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET ...
    # # WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT ...
    #
    # NOTE: SnowflakeOperator doesn't return row counts like the Hook.
    # If you need post-load validation, add a separate @task with a Hook.

    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # LEVEL 3: S3ToSnowflakeOperator (ALTERNATIVE — commented)
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # When: loading DATA FILES (parquet, csv) from S3 into a Snowflake table.
    #
    # HOW IT WORKS — the full picture:
    #
    #   1. Spark writes processed data as parquet FILES to S3:
    #      s3://insurance-processed/claims/2026-06-09/part-00000.parquet
    #      s3://insurance-processed/claims/2026-06-09/part-00001.parquet
    #
    #   2. Snowflake has an "external stage" = a pointer to that S3 path.
    #      (Created once by a DBA, not by the DAG):
    #
    #      CREATE STAGE claims_s3_stage
    #          URL = 's3://insurance-processed/'
    #          CREDENTIALS = (AWS_KEY_ID='...' AWS_SECRET_KEY='...');
    #
    #   3. S3ToSnowflakeOperator tells Snowflake:
    #      "read those parquet files from the stage → load as rows into table"
    #
    #      Under the hood it runs Snowflake's COPY INTO command:
    #      COPY INTO claims_staging.claims_raw
    #      FROM @claims_s3_stage/claims/2026-06-09/
    #      FILE_FORMAT = (TYPE=PARQUET)
    #
    #   4. Parquet files → rows in Snowflake table. Fast, parallel, bulk.
    #
    # VISUAL:
    #   [Spark writes parquet to S3]
    #          ↓
    #   s3://bucket/claims/2026-06-09/*.parquet    ← files on S3
    #          ↓
    #   S3ToSnowflakeOperator (COPY INTO)          ← Snowflake reads files
    #          ↓
    #   claims_staging.claims_raw                  ← now it's TABLE ROWS
    #          ↓
    #   SnowflakeOperator (MERGE INTO)             ← staging → warehouse
    #          ↓
    #   claims_warehouse.claims_daily              ← final table
    #
    # from airflow.providers.snowflake.transfers.s3_to_snowflake import S3ToSnowflakeOperator
    #
    # # Step A: COPY parquet files from S3 → Snowflake staging table
    # copy_to_staging = S3ToSnowflakeOperator(
    #     task_id="copy_s3_to_snowflake",
    #     snowflake_conn_id="snowflake_default",
    #     s3_keys=["claims/{{ ds }}/"],              # S3 prefix with parquet files
    #     table="claims_staging.claims_raw",          # target table in Snowflake
    #     schema="claims_staging",
    #     stage="claims_s3_stage",                    # external stage (created by DBA)
    #     file_format="(TYPE=PARQUET)",               # tells Snowflake the file format
    # )
    #
    # # Step B: MERGE from staging → warehouse (separate task)
    # merge_to_warehouse = SnowflakeOperator(
    #     task_id="merge_to_warehouse",
    #     snowflake_conn_id="snowflake_default",
    #     sql="include/sql/merge_claims.sql",
    # )
    #
    # # Wiring for Level 3:
    # # processed >> copy_to_staging >> merge_to_warehouse >> qc
    #
    # WHY 2 STEPS (COPY + MERGE)?
    # COPY INTO loads raw data into a staging table (fast, bulk, parallel).
    # MERGE moves it into the final warehouse table (idempotent, with business logic).
    # This is the standard "staging → warehouse" pattern.
    #
    # WHEN TO USE EACH LEVEL:
    # Level 1 (Hook):     Dynamic SQL, need Python logic, return values
    # Level 2 (Operator): Static SQL, clean separation, .sql files
    # Level 3 (Transfer): Bulk file loading from S3, highest performance

    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # STEP 8: QUALITY CHECK  (say: "After loading, I validate the
    #   output — this is the second half of the validation sandwich")
    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

    @task()
    def quality_check(load_info: dict) -> dict:
        """
        Post-load validation.
        Zero rows after load = silent failure, worse than a crash.
        """
        if load_info["row_count"] == 0:
            raise ValueError(f"ZERO rows loaded for {load_info['date']}!")

        # Could add more checks here:
        # - null percentage in key columns
        # - duplicate detection
        # - comparison with previous day's count (anomaly detection)

        logger.info("QC passed: %d rows for %s", load_info["row_count"], load_info["date"])
        return {
            "status": "passed",
            "row_count": load_info["row_count"],
            "date": load_info["date"],
        }

    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # STEP 9: NOTIFICATIONS  (say: "Finally, email alerts —
    #   success email if all good, failure email if anything broke")
    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

    notify_success = EmailOperator(
        task_id="notify_success",
        to=["data-team@company.com"],
        subject="Claims Pipeline {{ ds }} — SUCCESS",
        html_content="""
        <h3>Claims Pipeline Complete</h3>
        <ul>
            <li><b>Date:</b> {{ ds }}</li>
            <li><b>Rows loaded:</b> {{ ti.xcom_pull(task_ids='quality_check')['row_count'] }}</li>
        </ul>
        """,
        trigger_rule=TriggerRule.ALL_SUCCESS,     # only if everything passed
    )

    notify_failure = EmailOperator(
        task_id="notify_failure",
        to=["data-team@company.com"],
        subject="Claims Pipeline {{ ds }} — FAILED",
        html_content="<p>Claims pipeline failed. Check Airflow logs.</p>",
        trigger_rule=TriggerRule.ONE_FAILED,       # if ANY upstream failed
    )

    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # STEP 10: WIRING  (say: "Now I connect everything — this defines
    #   the execution order")
    # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    # Read top to bottom:
    # 1. Wait for file in S3
    # 2. Validate source (size check)
    # 3. Process with Spark
    # 4. Load into Snowflake (MERGE = idempotent)
    # 5. Quality check (row count > 0)
    # 6. Send success or failure email

    source = validate_source()
    wait_claims_file >> source              # sensor gates everything

    processed = process_claims(source)      # XCom: source info → Spark
    loaded = load_to_snowflake(processed)   # XCom: process output → Snowflake
    qc = quality_check(loaded)              # XCom: load info → QC

    qc >> notify_success
    qc >> notify_failure


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# DON'T FORGET: instantiate the DAG
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

#               WHAT THE INTERVIEWER WILL ASK — YOUR ANSWERS
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
"""
These are the SAME questions every time. Know these cold.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Q: "Why catchup=False?"
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
"If I deploy today with start_date in January, Airflow would try to
 backfill every missed day — hundreds of runs at once. catchup=False
 means: only run from now forward. For historical backfill, I trigger
 manually with controlled parallelism."

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Q: "Why max_active_runs=1?"
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
"Prevents overlapping runs. If today's run is slow and tomorrow's starts,
 they'd write to the same table simultaneously — race conditions,
 duplicate data. max_active_runs=1 means one at a time."

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Q: "Why depends_on_past=False?"
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
"If True, one failure blocks ALL future runs until someone manually
 clears it. False = each run is independent. Monday's failure doesn't
 block Tuesday. I handle dependencies with sensors and validation."

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Q: "Why mode='reschedule' on the sensor?"
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
"In 'poke' mode (default), the sensor holds a worker slot for hours
 doing nothing. 'reschedule' releases the slot between checks — other
 tasks can use it. Critical when you have limited workers."

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Q: "What's the difference between Operator, Sensor, and Hook?"
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
"Operators DO work — run a query, send email.
 Sensors WAIT for conditions — file exists, DAG finished.
 Hooks CONNECT to external systems — manage credentials + API calls.
 Operators and Sensors use Hooks under the hood."

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Q: "How do you pass data between tasks?"
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
"XCom. With TaskFlow API, it's automatic — a task's return value goes
 to XCom, and when I pass it as argument to the next task, Airflow
 pulls it. Key rule: only small data (paths, counts, status).
 Never DataFrames — XCom goes through the metadata database."

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Q: "What is idempotency and why does it matter?"
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
"Same result no matter how many times you run it. Critical because
 Airflow retries. If my load task uses INSERT, a retry duplicates data.
 I use MERGE/upsert — if the row exists, update it; if not, insert.
 That's why my Snowflake load uses MERGE, not INSERT."
 ↑↑↑ POINT TO YOUR CODE when saying this ↑↑↑

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Q: "Why validate BEFORE processing?"
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
"Fail fast = save money. If the source file is empty or missing, I don't
 want to spin up a Spark cluster for nothing. A head_object call costs
 fractions of a cent. A Spark job costs dollars."

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Q: "Why validate AFTER processing too?"
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
"Silent failures. A job can finish successfully but produce zero rows.
 Without a post-load check, you'd only discover it when a report is
 empty or a stakeholder complains. I catch it immediately."

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Q: "How would you make this reusable for 50 similar pipelines?"
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
"Three approaches, depending on complexity:
 1. DAG Factory: YAML config file defines each pipeline's source,
    schedule, and destination. A Python script generates DAGs from it.
 2. Custom Operators: extract repeated patterns (like S3→Snowflake load)
    into reusable operators the team imports.
 3. DAG templates: a base DAG class with standard validation, alerting,
    and retry config that teams extend for their specific logic."

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Q: "What executor would you use in production?"
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
"CeleryExecutor for distributed workers, or KubernetesExecutor if each
 task needs isolated resources. Since this role uses Astronomer, it
 likely uses KubernetesExecutor or CeleryExecutor out of the box —
 Astronomer manages the infrastructure."

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Q: "How do you handle secrets/credentials?"
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
"Never in code. Airflow Connections store credentials — I reference them
 by conn_id (like 'aws_default', 'snowflake_default'). For other config,
 Airflow Variables. On Astronomer, I'd also integrate with AWS Secrets
 Manager as a secrets backend."

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Q: "What about CI/CD?"
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
"Jenkins pipeline with stages:
 1. Lint (flake8) — catch syntax issues
 2. Test (pytest) — unit tests + DAG integrity test (import the DAG,
    check no import errors, check cycle-free)
 3. Deploy to staging — test on staging Airflow
 4. Deploy to prod — on Astronomer, this is 'astro deploy'"
"""

""" REALISTIC PRODUCTION DAG — Insurance Claims Pipeline This is what a Wizdaa/Capgemini DAG looks like in practice. Pattern: DAG = orchestrator (lightweight, metadata only) Heavy work = external scripts (spark-submit, python scripts) XCom = paths, counts, status (NEVER raw data) Study this for interviews. You can explain every piece. """ from datetime import datetime, timedelta from airflow.decorators import dag, task from airflow.operators.python import PythonOperator from airflow.providers.amazon.aws.sensors.s3 import S3KeySensor from airflow.providers.amazon.aws.hooks.s3 import S3Hook from airflow.providers.postgres.hooks.postgres import PostgresHook from airflow.sensors.external_task import ExternalTaskSensor from airflow.operators.email import EmailOperator from airflow.utils.trigger_rule import TriggerRule import subprocess import json import os # ============================================================ # CONFIG — no hardcoded values in DAG logic # ============================================================ RAW_BUCKET = "company-raw-data" PROCESSED_BUCKET = "company-processed-data" GOLD_BUCKET = "company-gold-data" SPARK_SCRIPTS = "/opt/airflow/spark_jobs" ENV = os.environ.get("ENVIRONMENT", "dev") # dev / staging / prod ALERT_EMAILS = ["data-team@company.com", "on-call@company.com"] DEFAULT_ARGS = { "owner": "data-engineering", "depends_on_past": False, "retries": 2, "retry_delay": timedelta(minutes=5), "retry_exponential_backoff": True, "max_retry_delay": timedelta(minutes=30), "email_on_failure": True, "email": ALERT_EMAILS, } # ============================================================ # HELPER FUNCTIONS — reusable across DAGs # ============================================================ def run_spark_job(script_name: str, args: list = None) -> dict: """ Submit Spark job and capture result. Returns metadata dict — NOT the data itself. This is the pattern: - DAG submits spark-submit - Spark script reads from S3, processes, writes to S3 - Script prints JSON metadata to stdout at the end - DAG captures that metadata via stdout parsing """ script_path = os.path.join(SPARK_SCRIPTS, script_name) cmd = [ "spark-submit", "--master", "yarn", "--deploy-mode", "client", "--conf", "spark.sql.shuffle.partitions=200", "--conf", "spark.executor.memory=4g", "--conf", "spark.executor.cores=4", "--conf", "spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled=true", script_path, ] + (args or []) print(f"[SPARK] Submitting: {' '.join(cmd)}") proc = subprocess.run( cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=7200, # 2 hour timeout ) if proc.returncode != 0: error_msg = proc.stderr[-2000:] if proc.stderr else "No stderr" raise RuntimeError(f"Spark job failed (exit {proc.returncode}): {error_msg}") # Parse metadata from last line of stdout (convention: script prints JSON) # Example output: {"output_path": "s3://...", "record_count": 50000, "status": "success"} stdout_lines = proc.stdout.strip().split("\n") for line in reversed(stdout_lines): try: metadata = json.loads(line) return metadata except json.JSONDecodeError: continue return {"status": "success", "output": proc.stdout[-500:]} def check_row_count(table: str, conn_id: str = "postgres_prod") -> int: """Quick row count check using Hook — no hardcoded credentials.""" hook = PostgresHook(postgres_conn_id=conn_id) result = hook.get_first(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {table}") return result[0] if result else 0 def validate_s3_output(bucket: str, prefix: str, min_files: int = 1) -> dict: """Check S3 output exists and has expected files.""" hook = S3Hook(aws_conn_id="aws_default") keys = hook.list_keys(bucket_name=bucket, prefix=prefix) file_count = len(keys) if keys else 0 if file_count < min_files: raise ValueError( f"Expected >= {min_files} files at s3://{bucket}/{prefix}, found {file_count}" ) # Calculate total size total_size = 0 for key in (keys or []): metadata = hook.head_object(key=key, bucket_name=bucket) total_size += metadata.get("ContentLength", 0) return { "path": f"s3://{bucket}/{prefix}", "file_count": file_count, "total_size_mb": round(total_size / (1024 * 1024), 2), } # ============================================================ # DAG DEFINITION — mixed classic + decorator style # ============================================================ @dag( dag_id="insurance_claims_daily_pipeline", default_args=DEFAULT_ARGS, description="Daily ETL: raw claims → bronze → silver → gold + quality checks", schedule="0 6 * * *", # 6 AM daily start_date=datetime(2025, 1, 1), catchup=False, max_active_runs=1, # prevent parallel runs tags=["insurance", "claims", "production", "daily"], ) def claims_pipeline(): # ======================================================== # PHASE 1: WAIT FOR DEPENDENCIES # Classic style — sensors don't have decorator equivalent # ======================================================== # Wait for upstream data provider to drop file in S3 # mode='reschedule' frees worker slot during long waits wait_raw_file = S3KeySensor( task_id="wait_raw_claims_file", bucket_name=RAW_BUCKET, bucket_key="claims/daily/{{ ds }}/claims_raw.json", # Jinja: execution date aws_conn_id="aws_default", poke_interval=300, # check every 5 min timeout=14400, # give up after 4 hours mode="reschedule", # free worker while waiting ) # Wait for reference data DAG to finish first wait_reference_data = ExternalTaskSensor( task_id="wait_reference_tables", external_dag_id="reference_data_daily_refresh", external_task_id="load_complete", execution_delta=timedelta(hours=1), # reference DAG runs at 5 AM timeout=3600, mode="reschedule", ) # ======================================================== # PHASE 2: SOURCE VALIDATION # Decorator style — pure Python, return metadata via XCom # ======================================================== @task() def validate_source(ds: str = None) -> dict: """ Check source file before processing — saves compute cost. If source is bad, fail BEFORE spinning up Spark cluster. ds parameter is automatically injected by Airflow (execution date). """ hook = S3Hook(aws_conn_id="aws_default") key = f"claims/daily/{ds}/claims_raw.json" # Check file exists and size metadata = hook.head_object(key=key, bucket_name=RAW_BUCKET) size_mb = metadata["ContentLength"] / (1024 * 1024) # Basic validations BEFORE spending money on Spark if size_mb < 0.001: raise ValueError(f"Source file too small ({size_mb:.4f} MB) — likely empty") if size_mb > 5000: raise ValueError(f"Source file too large ({size_mb:.1f} MB) — investigate") print(f"[VALIDATE] Source OK: {key} ({size_mb:.2f} MB)") return { "source_path": f"s3://{RAW_BUCKET}/{key}", "source_size_mb": round(size_mb, 2), "execution_date": ds, } # ======================================================== # PHASE 3: BRONZE → SILVER → GOLD (Spark jobs) # Each returns metadata — heavy logic in external scripts # ======================================================== @task() def ingest_bronze(source_info: dict) -> dict: """ Bronze: raw ingestion, minimal transformation. Spark script reads JSON from S3, writes Iceberg table. """ result = run_spark_job( "bronze_claims_ingest.py", args=[ "--source", source_info["source_path"], "--target", f"s3://{PROCESSED_BUCKET}/bronze/claims/{source_info['execution_date']}/", "--date", source_info["execution_date"], ], ) print(f"[BRONZE] Ingested {result.get('record_count', '?')} records") return { "bronze_path": result.get("output_path", ""), "record_count": result.get("record_count", 0), "execution_date": source_info["execution_date"], } @task() def transform_silver(bronze_info: dict) -> dict: """ Silver: cleaned, deduplicated, enriched with reference data. Spark script handles: dedup, null handling, joins, type casting. """ result = run_spark_job( "silver_claims_transform.py", args=[ "--source", bronze_info["bronze_path"], "--target", f"s3://{PROCESSED_BUCKET}/silver/claims/{bronze_info['execution_date']}/", "--date", bronze_info["execution_date"], ], ) print(f"[SILVER] Transformed: {result.get('valid_records', '?')} valid, " f"{result.get('quarantined', '?')} quarantined") return { "silver_path": result.get("output_path", ""), "valid_records": result.get("valid_records", 0), "quarantined": result.get("quarantined", 0), "execution_date": bronze_info["execution_date"], } @task() def aggregate_gold(silver_info: dict) -> dict: """ Gold: business-ready aggregations. Spark script builds: daily summary, KPIs, dimensional model. """ result = run_spark_job( "gold_claims_aggregate.py", args=[ "--source", silver_info["silver_path"], "--target", f"s3://{GOLD_BUCKET}/claims_summary/{silver_info['execution_date']}/", "--date", silver_info["execution_date"], ], ) print(f"[GOLD] Aggregated: {result.get('output_records', '?')} summary records") return { "gold_path": result.get("output_path", ""), "output_records": result.get("output_records", 0), "execution_date": silver_info["execution_date"], } # ======================================================== # PHASE 4: DATA QUALITY CHECKS # Validate AFTER processing — catch silent failures # ======================================================== @task() def quality_check_silver(silver_info: dict) -> dict: """ Validate Silver output: - File exists in S3 - Record count within expected range - No excessive quarantine (> 5% = alert) """ # Check S3 output output_info = validate_s3_output( PROCESSED_BUCKET, f"silver/claims/{silver_info['execution_date']}/", min_files=1, ) # Check quarantine ratio total = silver_info["valid_records"] + silver_info["quarantined"] quarantine_pct = (silver_info["quarantined"] / total * 100) if total > 0 else 0 if quarantine_pct > 5.0: print(f"⚠️ WARNING: {quarantine_pct:.1f}% records quarantined — investigate source") if silver_info["valid_records"] == 0: raise ValueError("ZERO valid records in Silver — pipeline broken!") return { "status": "passed", "valid_records": silver_info["valid_records"], "quarantine_pct": round(quarantine_pct, 2), "output_size_mb": output_info["total_size_mb"], } @task() def quality_check_gold(gold_info: dict) -> dict: """Validate Gold output exists and has records.""" output_info = validate_s3_output( GOLD_BUCKET, f"claims_summary/{gold_info['execution_date']}/", min_files=1, ) if gold_info["output_records"] == 0: raise ValueError("ZERO records in Gold layer!") return { "status": "passed", "output_records": gold_info["output_records"], "output_size_mb": output_info["total_size_mb"], } # ======================================================== # PHASE 5: NOTIFICATION # Classic style — EmailOperator with Jinja templates # ======================================================== notify_success = EmailOperator( task_id="notify_success", to=ALERT_EMAILS, subject="[{{ var.value.env }}] Claims Pipeline {{ ds }} ✅ SUCCESS", html_content="""

Claims Pipeline Completed Successfully

  • Date: {{ ds }}
  • Silver records: {{ ti.xcom_pull(task_ids='quality_check_silver')['valid_records'] }}
  • Quarantine %: {{ ti.xcom_pull(task_ids='quality_check_silver')['quarantine_pct'] }}%
  • Gold records: {{ ti.xcom_pull(task_ids='quality_check_gold')['output_records'] }}
""", trigger_rule=TriggerRule.ALL_SUCCESS, ) notify_failure = EmailOperator( task_id="notify_failure", to=ALERT_EMAILS, subject="[{{ var.value.env }}] Claims Pipeline {{ ds }} ❌ FAILED", html_content="""

Claims Pipeline FAILED

Check Airflow logs for details.

Execution date: {{ ds }}

""", trigger_rule=TriggerRule.ONE_FAILED, # runs if ANY upstream failed ) # ======================================================== # WIRING — dependency chain # ======================================================== # Phase 1: wait for dependencies (parallel sensors) source_info = validate_source() [wait_raw_file, wait_reference_data] >> source_info # both must complete # Phase 2-3: Bronze → Silver → Gold (sequential, data flows via XCom) bronze = ingest_bronze(source_info) silver = transform_silver(bronze) gold = aggregate_gold(silver) # Phase 4: quality checks (parallel — silver and gold independent) qc_silver = quality_check_silver(silver) qc_gold = quality_check_gold(gold) # Phase 5: notifications (after quality checks) [qc_silver, qc_gold] >> notify_success [qc_silver, qc_gold] >> notify_failure # Instantiate claims_pipeline() """ VISUAL FLOW: [wait_raw_file] ──┐ ├──→ [validate_source] → [bronze] → [silver] → [gold] [wait_ref_data] ──┘ │ │ ▼ ▼ [qc_silver] [qc_gold] │ │ ├──────────┤ ▼ ▼ [notify_success] [notify_failure] KEY PATTERNS: 1. Sensors wait for external dependencies (files, other DAGs) 2. validate_source checks BEFORE expensive Spark jobs (cost saving) 3. Each Spark task returns METADATA only (paths, counts) 4. Heavy logic lives in external scripts (bronze/silver/gold .py files) 5. Quality checks validate AFTER processing 6. Dual notifications: success OR failure (trigger_rule) 7. XCom passes metadata between tasks automatically (decorator style) 8. max_active_runs=1 prevents parallel DAG runs WHAT INTERVIEWERS WANT TO HEAR: - "DAG is lightweight — orchestration only, no heavy logic" - "External scripts do the processing, DAG captures metadata" - "Sensors use reschedule mode for long waits to free worker slots" - "Quality checks before AND after processing" - "Hooks manage connections — no hardcoded credentials" - "Medallion architecture: Bronze (raw) → Silver (clean) → Gold (aggregated)" """

cards.answer:
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*- """ IMPROVED VERSION — dag_carga_metas_2instancia.py Changes from original: 1. Added Sensor: wait for orchestrator/upstream before running 2. Mixed decorator + classic style (modern Airflow 2.x) 3. Added source validation BEFORE submitting expensive EMR step 4. Added post-execution quality check 5. Added email notification (success + failure) 6. Added EmrStepSensor instead of wait_for_completion (more control) 7. Better error handling with descriptive XCom metadata 8. Added execution_timeout to prevent runaway steps Original: inicio → validar_cluster → montar_step → executar → fim Improved: wait_upstream → validate_cluster → validate_source → submit_step → monitor_step → quality_check → [notify_success | notify_failure] """ import logging from datetime import datetime, timedelta import boto3 import pendulum from airflow import DAG from airflow.decorators import task from airflow.models import Variable from airflow.operators.empty import EmptyOperator from airflow.operators.python import PythonOperator from airflow.operators.email import EmailOperator from airflow.providers.amazon.aws.operators.emr import EmrAddStepsOperator from airflow.providers.amazon.aws.sensors.emr import EmrStepSensor from airflow.sensors.external_task import ExternalTaskSensor from airflow.utils.trigger_rule import TriggerRule logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) # ========================================================= # CONFIG — resolved at execution time, NOT parse time # ========================================================= DAG_ID = "dag_carga_metas_2instancia" TZ = pendulum.timezone("America/Sao_Paulo") CLUSTER_VAR_KEY = "EMR_CLUSTER_PROJETOS_2INST" AWS_CONN_ID = "aws_default" SCHEDULE = None # triggered by orchestrator DAG ALERT_EMAILS = [ "felipe.lisboa@tjrj.jus.br", ] default_args = { "owner": "data-engineering", "depends_on_past": False, "retries": 1, "retry_delay": timedelta(minutes=2), "email_on_failure": True, "email": ALERT_EMAILS, } # ========================================================= # HELPER — keep Variable.get() inside functions # ========================================================= def _aws_region() -> str: return Variable.get("aws_region", default_var="sa-east-1") # ========================================================= # DAG # ========================================================= with DAG( dag_id=DAG_ID, start_date=pendulum.datetime(2026, 4, 19, tz=TZ), schedule=SCHEDULE, catchup=False, max_active_runs=1, default_args=default_args, tags=["projeto", "metacnj", "emr", "2inst", "meta"], ) as dag: inicio = EmptyOperator(task_id="inicio") # ======================================================== # 1: Sensor — wait for upstream DAG # ======================================================== wait_upstream = ExternalTaskSensor( task_id="wait_upstream_orchestrator", external_dag_id="dag_orquestradora_2instancia", external_task_id="trigger_metas_ready", timeout=3600, mode="reschedule", poke_interval=60, ) # ======================================================== # 2: Validate cluster - pushes cluster_id + state as structured metadata # ======================================================== @task() def validar_cluster() -> dict: """Validate EMR cluster is ready for steps.""" cluster_id = Variable.get(CLUSTER_VAR_KEY, default_var="").strip() if not cluster_id: raise ValueError(f"Variable {CLUSTER_VAR_KEY} is empty — set it in Airflow UI") emr = boto3.client("emr", region_name=_aws_region()) resp = emr.describe_cluster(ClusterId=cluster_id) state = resp["Cluster"]["Status"]["State"] name = resp["Cluster"]["Name"] if state not in ("WAITING", "RUNNING"): raise RuntimeError( f"Cluster {cluster_id} ({name}) state={state} — cannot submit steps. " f"Expected WAITING or RUNNING." ) logger.info("Cluster %s (%s) validated. State=%s", cluster_id, name, state) return { "cluster_id": cluster_id, "cluster_name": name, "cluster_state": state, } # ======================================================== # 3: Validate source - check if S3 script exists BEFORE submitting EMR step # ======================================================== @task() def validar_fonte(cluster_info: dict, **kwargs) -> dict: """ Validate inputs BEFORE submitting EMR step. Fail fast = save money (no wasted cluster time). """ import boto3 script_s3_path = Variable.get( "s3_script_metas_2instancia", default_var="s3://sgdai-projetos/2instancia/2inst_metacnj/run_all_metas_emr.py", ) # Parse S3 path parts = script_s3_path.replace("s3://", "").split("/", 1) bucket, key = parts[0], parts[1] # Check script exists on S3 s3 = boto3.client("s3", region_name=_aws_region()) try: s3.head_object(Bucket=bucket, Key=key) logger.info("Script found: %s", script_s3_path) except s3.exceptions.ClientError: raise FileNotFoundError(f"Script NOT found on S3: {script_s3_path}") year = kwargs["execution_date"].year dry_run = Variable.get("metacnj_dry_run", default_var="false").strip().lower() in ( "true", "1", "yes", "y", ) return { "cluster_id": cluster_info["cluster_id"], "script_s3_path": script_s3_path, "year": year, "dry_run": dry_run, } # ======================================================== # 4: Build step as structured task # Returns step list for EmrAddStepsOperator # ======================================================== @task() def montar_step(source_info: dict) -> list: """Build EMR step command.""" comando = ( f"hadoop fs -copyToLocal -f {source_info['script_s3_path']} /tmp/run_all_metas_emr.py " f"&& python3 /tmp/run_all_metas_emr.py --year {source_info['year']}" ) if source_info["dry_run"]: comando += " --dry-run" step = [ { "Name": f"2inst_metacnj_full_pipeline_{source_info['year']}", "ActionOnFailure": "CONTINUE", "HadoopJarStep": { "Jar": "command-runner.jar", "Args": ["bash", "-c", comando], }, } ] logger.info("Step built. dry_run=%s, year=%s", source_info["dry_run"], source_info["year"]) return step # ======================================================== # EMR execution — operator needs template fields # ======================================================== executar_pipeline = EmrAddStepsOperator( task_id="executar_pipeline_metas", job_flow_id="{{ ti.xcom_pull(task_ids='validar_cluster') ['cluster_id'] }}", aws_conn_id=AWS_CONN_ID, steps="{{ ti.xcom_pull(task_ids='montar_step') }}", wait_for_completion=False, ) # ======================================================== # 5: EmrStepSensor — separate monitoring # Better than wait_for_completion because: # - Configurable poke_interval # - mode='reschedule' frees worker slot # - Separate task = clearer Airflow UI visibility # ======================================================== monitorar_step = EmrStepSensor( task_id="monitorar_step_emr", job_flow_id="{{ ti.xcom_pull(task_ids='validar_cluster')['cluster_id'] }}", step_id="{{ ti.xcom_pull(task_ids='executar_pipeline_metas')[0] }}", aws_conn_id=AWS_CONN_ID, mode="reschedule", # free worker while EMR runs poke_interval=30, # check every 30s timeout=36000, # 10 hours max ) # ======================================================== # 6: Post-execution quality check # Verify EMR step actually produced expected output # ======================================================== @task() def quality_check(**kwargs) -> dict: """ After EMR completes, verify output tables """ import boto3 year = kwargs["execution_date"].year # Check if Iceberg tables were updated glue = boto3.client("glue", region_name=_aws_region()) tables_to_check = [ "tb_meta01", "tb_meta02", "tb_meta04", "tb_meta06", "tb_meta07", "tb_meta08", "tb_meta10", "tb_meta11", ] results = {} for table in tables_to_check: try: resp = glue.get_table(DatabaseName="dw2inst", Name=table) update_time = resp["Table"].get("UpdateTime") results[table] = { "exists": True, "last_updated": str(update_time) if update_time else "unknown", } except glue.exceptions.EntityNotFoundException: results[table] = {"exists": False} logger.warning("Table %s NOT found in Glue catalog!", table) missing = [t for t, info in results.items() if not info["exists"]] if missing: raise ValueError(f"Missing tables after pipeline: {missing}") logger.info("Quality check passed. All %d tables exist.", len(tables_to_check)) return { "status": "passed", "tables_checked": len(tables_to_check), "year": year, } # ======================================================== # 7: Notifications # ======================================================== notify_success = EmailOperator( task_id="notify_success", to=ALERT_EMAILS, subject="[2INST][META CNJ] Pipeline {{ execution_date.year }} ✅ SUCESSO", html_content="""

Pipeline de Metas CNJ 2ª Instância concluído com sucesso.

  • Ano: {{ execution_date.year }}
  • Cluster: {{ ti.xcom_pull(task_ids='validar_cluster')['cluster_id'] }}
  • Tabelas verificadas: {{ ti.xcom_pull(task_ids='quality_check')['tables_checked'] }}
""", trigger_rule=TriggerRule.ALL_SUCCESS, ) notify_failure = EmailOperator( task_id="notify_failure", to=ALERT_EMAILS, subject="[2INST][META CNJ] Pipeline {{ execution_date.year }} ❌ ERRO", html_content="""

Pipeline de Metas CNJ falhou. Verifique os logs no Airflow.

Cluster: {{ ti.xcom_pull(task_ids='validar_cluster')['cluster_id'] or 'N/A' }}

""", trigger_rule=TriggerRule.ONE_FAILED, ) fim = EmptyOperator( task_id="fim", trigger_rule=TriggerRule.NONE_FAILED_MIN_ONE_SUCCESS, ) # ======================================================== # WIRING # ======================================================== # Validate phase cluster_info = validar_cluster() source_info = validar_fonte(cluster_info) step = montar_step(source_info) inicio >> wait_upstream >> cluster_info # Execute phase step >> executar_pipeline executar_pipeline >> monitorar_step # Quality + notification phase qc = quality_check() monitorar_step >> qc qc >> notify_success >> fim qc >> notify_failure >> fim """ COMPARISON: Original vs Improved Original: inicio → validar_cluster → montar_step → executar (wait_for_completion=True) → fim ✅ Simple, works ❌ No upstream sensor ❌ No source validation (script exists on S3?) ❌ No quality check after execution ❌ No email notification ❌ wait_for_completion blocks worker slot Improved: inicio → wait_upstream → validar_cluster → validar_fonte → montar_step → executar (no wait) → monitorar_step (sensor, reschedule) → quality_check → [notify_success | notify_failure] → fim ✅ Sensor waits for upstream DAG ✅ Validates S3 script exists BEFORE submitting (fail fast = save money) ✅ EmrStepSensor with reschedule mode (frees worker) ✅ Quality check verifies output tables exist in Glue catalog ✅ Email notifications on success AND failure ✅ Mixed decorator + classic style (modern pattern) ✅ Structured metadata flows via XCom """
